225.t: Granz's philosophy: jam sessions and the blues

87.t: Granz's first jam sessions in Los Angeles
87.s: Granz ran small sessions in L.A. paying $9; Young, Willie Smith, Nat Cole and Red Callender played, and Granz later paid well and traveled first class.
87.q: Norman, he was just running little jazz sessions out at the True Building. He's giving -- he'd give us (unintelligible) come into L.A. And he just finished UCLA, and when we'd come in L.A. he would try to run these sessions. And he'd give us $9.00 to go out there. And he had the money to play these…

87.s: He made two tours of eight to ten weeks, not two years; Granz kept only Ella and Oscar Peterson steadily.
87.q: Just tours -- just parts of those two years, the spots -- a tour wouldn't last over eight or ten weeks, you know, so I made two tours with him really, two tours would sound better than two years, because Norman never kept anything going for two years. 416.t: Jazz at the Philharmonic and Norman Granz's all-star roster
416.s: After Herman's band broke up in 1946 he joined Granz for eleven years; he lists the tenors, trumpets, rhythm players, singers and altos on the tours.
416.q: Yeah. That’s after the big bands started to break up. Woody broke up in 1946, and I joined. Norman called me and I came in in 1946 in September we started. 153.t: Touring with JATP; Oscar as the 'padrone'
